name: Sweden

facts.religion: Lutheran church members about 52%, largely secular

snapshot: Sweden's left-leaning bloc won a narrow majority in September 2026, but forming a government has dragged on, leaving Ulf Kristersson as caretaker.
culture: Sweden gave the world ABBA, IKEA, Spotify, Astrid Lindgren and the Nobel Prizes. Midsummer, fika coffee breaks and the concept of lagom, just enough, are cultural touchstones. Allemansrätten, the right to roam, gives everyone access to nature.
society: Sweden has a generous welfare state and high equality, but gang shootings and bombings have made it an outlier in Europe for gun violence. Immigration, which changed the country fast, is a central political debate. It joined NATO in 2024, ending two centuries of military non-alignment.
situation: For four years, Sweden was governed by a centre-right coalition that depended on the votes of the Sweden Democrats, a party with roots in the neo-Nazi movement that became the country's second largest. It was a historic break in a country long seen as Europe's model of social democracy, and the government took a hard line on immigration and gang crime. In September, Swedes narrowly reversed it, and then found that winning was the easy part.

In the 13 September election, the four left-leaning parties won 176 of 349 seats against 173 for Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's bloc, and the Sweden Democrats lost ground, putting Sweden at odds with the far-right rise across much of Europe (L'Orient-Le Jour). Kristersson resigned on 17 September, and the speaker asked Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson, Sweden's first woman prime minister in 2021-22, to form a government (Euronews). Her bloc was fractured: the Centre Party and the Left Party disagree sharply. On 28 September, after the Left Party backed a centre-right candidate for speaker, Andersson said there was "currently no possibility" for her to form a government (Reuters via Oman Observer). The speaker can put up to four candidates to a vote; if all fail, Sweden must hold a new election. Kristersson stays on as caretaker.
power: A constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system of "negative parliamentarism": a prime minister takes office unless an absolute majority of the 349-seat Riksdag votes against. King Carl XVI Gustaf is ceremonial.
holders: Caretaker Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson (Moderates), while government formation continues.
